title: Links and Anchors
summary: Create links with anchor elements and useful link text.

sketchBlocks.title: A link needs a destination and useful text
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: The anchor element creates a link. Its `href` attribute stores the destination, while the text between the tags tells the learner what the link does. ```html Advising resources ``` `href` is an attribute on the opening `` tag. The visible phrase **Advising resources** is better than vague text such as "click here" because it explains the destination.

sketchBlocks.title: Fragment links jump to an id on the same page
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A fragment destination begins with `#` and matches an `id` value elsewhere in the document. ```html Jump to the schedule

Tutoring schedule

Drop-in tutoring runs Monday through Thursday.

``` Line by line: **First**, the anchor points to `#schedule`, which names a location on the current page. **Second**, the `

` creates that destination by using `id="schedule"`. **Third**, the paragraph supplies the content that belongs under the heading. The browser can now connect the link to the matching target without loading another HTML file.

sketchBlocks.title: Choose destinations and link text deliberately
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A full web address such as `https://example.org/...` points to an external destination. A fragment such as `#clubs` points within the current page. ```html

Jump to student clubs

Visit the library guide

``` Line by line: **First**, the opening paragraph groups a same-page navigation link. **Second**, that anchor uses a fragment destination so the browser stays on the current document. **Third**, the next paragraph groups a separate external link. **Fourth**, the final anchor uses a complete web address, so the destination does not depend on the current file's folder. Meaningful anchor text tells the learner why each destination is useful.

quizDraft.title: Identify the link destination
quizDraft.prompt: Which part of an anchor element tells the browser where the link goes?
quizDraft.hint: Think about the job performed by each part of the opening anchor tag.

help.concept: An anchor separates navigation information from the clickable label.
help.hint_1: Look inside the opening tag for the piece that stores the destination.
help.hint_2: Eliminate choices that represent elements or unrelated identifiers.

quizDraft.title: Choose a same-page link
quizDraft.prompt: Which href points to an element whose id is `resources` on the current page?
quizDraft.hint: A same-page fragment starts with a hash character.

help.concept: Fragment links pair href='#name' with id='name'.
help.hint_1: The hash tells the browser this is a fragment identifier.
help.hint_2: The characters after # must match the target id.

quizDraft.title: Recognize useful links
quizDraft.prompt: Which practices make an HTML link understandable and functional? Choose all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Think about both the destination and what the learner sees.

help.concept: A useful link combines a valid destination with descriptive text.
help.hint_1: Fragment links also need a matching id target.
help.hint_2: Vague link text removes useful context.

options: Give the anchor meaningful visible text.
Make every link text say only 'click here'.
Match a fragment href with a target id.

quizDraft.title: Build a fragment link and target
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the lines so the link appears before the heading it targets.
quizDraft.hint: The link can appear earlier on the page, then the matching id marks its target.

help.concept: Fragment navigation connects href='#resources' to id='resources'.
help.hint_1: Place the jump link before the destination in this exercise.
help.hint_2: The paragraph belongs below the Resources heading.

quizDraft.title: Complete an href
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the attribute name that stores the destination.
quizDraft.hint: Focus on the part of an opening anchor tag that pairs a name with a URL value.

help.concept: Anchor destinations are stored as an attribute-value pair in the opening tag.
help.hint_1: The blank is the attribute name immediately before the URL.
help.hint_2: Choose the navigation-related attribute rather than an element name.

quizDraft.title: Complete a fragment destination
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the href value that targets `id="contact"` on this page.
quizDraft.hint: A fragment destination adds # before the target id.

help.concept: Same-page fragment href values begin with #.
help.hint_2: Combine the hash with the id value.

quizDraft.title: Link to the real About page
quizDraft.prompt: Use the Explorer to confirm `about.html` is part of the site. In `index.html`, make the `About me` anchor navigate to that page. Use Preview and click the link to verify the second page opens.
quizDraft.hint: The destination is a page beside the current file.

help.concept: An anchor can connect one HTML document to another document in the same website.
help.hint_1: Keep the visible link text and add the destination to the opening anchor tag.
help.hint_2: The target page is already present beside the home page in Explorer.

quizDraft.title: Link to a page inside a folder
quizDraft.prompt: The site now includes `projects/robotics.html`. In `index.html`, connect the `Robotics project` anchor to that real nested page. Click it in Preview after you edit the link.
quizDraft.hint: The destination sits inside the projects folder.

help.concept: Anchor destinations can include folder segments when another page is nested inside the website.
help.hint_1: Read the file tree from the site root to the robotics page.
help.hint_2: Keep the existing About link unchanged while you connect the project link.

quizDraft.title: Add the return link on About
quizDraft.prompt: Open `about.html` from the Explorer. Make `Back to profile` navigate to the home page. Preview the About page, then use the link to return to the profile.
quizDraft.hint: Both HTML files are in the same folder.

help.concept: Multi-page sites usually provide links in both directions so learners can navigate between related pages.
help.hint_1: Edit the anchor in the About page, not the home page.
help.hint_2: The destination is the site's entry HTML file beside the About page.
